name: James Smith

events.title: Petition for 2,000 acres (candidate)
events.description: Petition of 'James Smith' for 2,000 acres of vacant land; survey 14 Dec 1722 of 2,000 acres in Ulster Co. (part of the vacated Capt. John Evans grant, adjoining Thomas Noxen and Patrick MacKnight). Weygant (1897) attributes this to James Smith of Moriches. Identity not proven.

events.title: Marriage
events.description: Married Jerusha, daughter of Elnathan Topping Jr. (Weygant); eldest son Matthew b. 3 Sept 1721 (Pelletreau)

bioAdditions:
Pelletreau (1898) lists James among Job Smith's children (Job 2d, 'Saint' Richard, Timothy, Aaron, James, Joseph, Elizabeth). He says James 'settled in Moriches' and married Jerusha Topping, and that their eldest child Matthew was born 3 Sept 1721 (S1). The 1688 family deed names only four sons of Job (Job, Richard, Joseph, Timothy), which fits James being born in or after 1688 (S4). Weygant's Family Record (1897) independently dates the marriage 'about the year 1720' and calls Jerusha a daughter of Elnathan Topping Jr. (S2). Weygant also credits James with a 1722 patent for 2,000 acres of the annulled Capt. John Evans grant in Ulster (now Orange) County, which the family apparently never settled. The Calendar of Land Papers confirms a 1721 petition and a 1722 survey for 'James Smith' (S3), but nothing in the calendar entry ties that James Smith to Moriches. Treat it as a candidate. If correct, it shows the family's interest in the Highlands a generation before Austin, Francis and Temperance moved to Woodbury Clove.

The tree names James's father as 'Justice Adam Smith (1649-1726)'. Pelletreau prints Adam Smith's will of 12 June 1704, which leaves all his estate to 'his only son Edmund Smith' (S5). Adam therefore had no son James, and the tree's link is wrong: James was the son of Job Smith & Elizabeth Thompson.

conflicts.foundValue: Job Smith (Pelletreau App. p. 478; Weygant p. 144); Adam Smith's 1704 will names an only son, Edmund
conflicts.assessment: Adam is disproven as James's father. Use Job Smith.

relationships.evidence: Listed as son of Job Smith by Pelletreau and Weygant; Adam (the tree's alternative) had an only son, Edmund

openQuestionsNew: Is the 1721/22 Evans-patent 'James Smith' the Moriches man? Check the original Land Papers (NY State Archives, vol. 60/63) for a residence.
WikiTree says '10 Oct 1740 James Smith of Moriches bought land in St. George's Manor of Captain Isaac Halsey'. Find the deed, which conflicts with his supposed 1740 death.

researchLogEntry: Round 4: Adam Smith's 1704 will (only son Edmund) disproves the tree's 'Justice Adam Smith' as father; Weygant 1897 and the 1864 Land Papers calendar add a candidate 1721-22 Ulster patent.
